solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cable television broadcast without Elvis on show

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, and without says some letters are taken away from the scrambled pool

parts.note: the letters of these two words form the pool
these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A cable TV schedule that, unusually, has no Elvis film in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the fifteen letters of CABLE TELEVISION, remove those of ELVIS, and rearrange the ten that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on show is visible to all, so it can easily be seen or spotted.

clue.text: For beak, rope's heartless

indicators.note: heartless asks for the central letter of the word for rope to be taken out

parts.note: a noose is a loop of rope; the 's is just 'is' linking to the indicator

explanation.surface: An odd swap: a bird's beak offered in exchange for a rope with no middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Beak is slang for the human snout, a synonym for the organ of smell.

clue.text: After time, safe to embrace strange bird

indicators.note: to embrace says the pair holds the next piece between them
safe comes after time, so the word for safe is placed to the right of T

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
rum is British informal for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone, after a while, keeping a strange bird safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Safecrackers were once called petermen, from peter for a safe. 'to embrace' says time and safe together surround strange, which sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter swan, or the South American trumpeter, is a type of bird named for its call.

clue.text: Mechanism blocked by church?

indicators.note: blocked by says the word for mechanism has something stuck inside it

parts.note: a contraption is a gadget or device
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A question about some device being forbidden by church authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: birth control is a mechanism that some churches forbid, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth control, which the Catholic church prohibits, is a method of preventing pregnancy, fitting a mechanism the church blocks.

clue.text: Gold colour for good sign

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to spice something up is to give it colour or interest

explanation.surface: Seeing a golden hue as a good omen.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is an omen, usually a favourable one, from Roman bird-watching for portents.

clue.text: Singer immortalised in rock

parts.note: the Rhine siren of legend, who lured boatmen with her song, is named after a tall rock on the river, and she lives on in that rock

explanation.surface: A rock star made immortal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests rock music, but it is a real crag on the Rhine, from which the legendary siren sang.
explanation.definitionFit: German legend tells of a siren singing on a Rhine cliff that bears her name, luring sailors to wreck.

clue.text: Theatrical group

definitions.meaning: exaggerated and showy in manner, affectedly flamboyant
a faction or party sharing a view, as in the opposing sides of a debate

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both affectedly showy and a faction holding a shared position.

clue.text: Crucial economy admitted by hospital department

indicators.note: admitted by says the department's letters take in the next piece, as a hospital admits a patient

parts.note: A and E is the accident and emergency department of a British hospital
a cut is a saving or economy

explanation.surface: Budget cuts being accepted by a hospital department at a critical time.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute situation is a critical or severe one, so the word fits crucial in the sense of decisive.

clue.text: Pressure on judge accepting new criminal's first bent

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: accepting says the word for judge takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: a referee judges a match

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of criminal

explanation.surface: Pressure on a judge to go easy on a crooked new defendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like the British slang for corrupt, chiming with criminal, but here it means an inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination or liking for something, much as a favourite leaning is a liking.

clue.text: Ignore tabloid regularly including pair…

indicators.note: regularly says the two inserted letters alternate with those of the paper
including says the newspaper's name takes letters inside it

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
PR is the abbreviation for pair, as on price tags for shoes
the second letter of the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: Choosing to disregard a tabloid, here a pair of stories, which trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly including' slots P and R alternately among S, U, N rather than as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject or disregard with contempt, a forceful way to ignore.

clue.text: Bible's definite about one in empty tomb

indicators.note: about says the word for definite goes round the rest

parts.note: being sure is being certain or definite

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the emptied vault
empty clears out the word's only vowel-like letter

parts.note: a crypt is an underground burial vault
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Bible-based certainty about someone in the empty tomb, the Easter story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' takes out the tomb word's only vowel, its Y, leaving CRPT; the I goes in, and 'about' wraps the certainty word round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Writ is another name for the Bible's text, the sacred writings of Christianity.

clue.text: I say 'stick' following declaration

indicators.note: following says the word for stick comes after the first piece

parts.note: I is a pronoun, as is said of it in grammar, so I, say, is an example
cement is used to stick things together

explanation.surface: Someone saying 'stick' after an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' is not the exclamation: it means 'I, for example', a part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An official statement or proclamation is a formal declaration of a view or decision.

clue.text: Unjust power replacing head of military

indicators.note: replacing head of says the first letter of the military word is swapped out

parts.note: martial means relating to war or the military
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An unfair power grab ousting the army's leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Being partial means favouring one side, which is biased and so unjust.

clue.text: Round gong struck excessively, initially

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of struck and excessively

explanation.surface: Someone hitting a gong too hard, too early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like an adjective for the gong, but it is the definition: plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Round in the sense of plump or tubby describes someone very overweight.

clue.text: Fuel Rover's last foreign car in factory

indicators.note: in says the letters go inside the word for factory

parts.note: a plant is a factory

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the British car name Rover

parts.note: Opel is a German car maker

explanation.surface: Fuel for a Rover and a foreign car in a car plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover was a British car make, a decoy beside OPEL; only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket's thrust comes from a propellant, a fuel or explosive charge that drives it.

clue.text: Headless 'thing' outside one's furthest lines of sight

indicators.note: outside says the shortened word goes round the next letter
Headless says the first letter of the word for thing is lost

parts.note: an article is an object or thing

indicators.note: furthest picks the last letter of one

explanation.surface: A decapitated object lying beyond the furthest point of one's vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticle is the grid of crosshairs in a telescope or gunsight, the fine lines that guide aiming.

clue.text: Quarantine island, run down, containing nothing

indicators.note: containing says the criticism word holds the next letter

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly or run down
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An island being run down while it holds no infection.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine someone is to keep them apart from others, cut off to stop disease spreading.

clue.text: Creature's weak, covered by wing flap

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the noun creature

parts.note: a wing of an organisation is an arm

indicators.note: covered by says the wing and flap words enclose the weak word

parts.note: a flap is a fuss or ado
ill means sick and weak

explanation.surface: An animal is feeble, its wing flapping as cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas, a specific example of a creature.

clue.text: 'Wall', backing Wright's ultimate record, a hit

indicators.note: backing says the whole string is read from end to start
ultimate takes the final letter of Wright

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a rap is a knock or hit

explanation.surface: A Wall by Wright backing a record that's a hit, like a pop chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns TEPARAP round. 'Wall' in quotes hints at a song title, but it is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along a roof, bridge or battlement edge.

clue.text: Bird's support missing top ends of tape measure

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird; the 's just joins it on

indicators.note: missing top says the first letter of the support word goes

parts.note: a bra is a support garment

indicators.note: ends of takes the first and last letters of tape

explanation.surface: A bird's support, minus its top, at the ends of a tape measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tape measure' looks like one object, but 'measure' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To titrate is to measure the concentration of a solution by adding a reagent until a reaction completes.

clue.text: Powerful detectives hold a multitude back

indicators.note: back says the whole combination is read from end to start
hold says the detectives' letters surround the number word

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
many means a multitude, a great number

explanation.surface: Strong police officers keeping a crowd back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole of CMANYID round, not just MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means full of energy and force, so vigorous and powerful.

clue.text: Scared by dead relative, heartless Dane flipped

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
an aunt is a relative

indicators.note: flipped says the remaining pair of letters is read in reverse
heartless removes the middle letters of Dane, keeping its outer pair

explanation.surface: Frightened by a dead relative, a heartless Dane, perhaps Hamlet, flips out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be daunted is to be intimidated or discouraged, so made afraid.

clue.text: Fruit in bowl I chilled…

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of words bowl I chilled

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit in a bowl that someone chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: The lichi, more often spelt lychee, is a Chinese fruit with sweet white flesh.

clue.text: Called distinguished in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word for distinguished is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: to distinguish something is to make it out, to see it

explanation.surface: Someone being named, called distinguished, in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distinguished' reads like a compliment, but it means 'made out by eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be summoned to appear in court, or named, is to be quoted or called, especially as a witness.

clue.text: …covered with syrup!

parts.note: syrup is rhyming slang: syrup of figs means wig, so being covered with syrup means wearing a hairpiece

explanation.surface: Following the fruit clue, a chilled lichi drenched in syrup, as a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the fruit clue so syrup looks sweet; it is Cockney rhyming slang (syrup of figs = wig).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing a hairpiece has their bald head covered by false hair, which rhyming slang calls a syrup.

clue.text: Jack rabbit grabbing rabbit's tail's male

indicators.note: grabbing says the reversed word holds the next letter
to jack is to lift up, and in a down clue lifting reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for chatter, as is gas

indicators.note: tail picks the last letter of rabbit

explanation.surface: A jackrabbit, grabbing a rabbit's tail, is male.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack rabbit' looks like the hare, but 'Jack' means jack up, turning GAS into SAG in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and by extension a man on his own, so a male.

clue.text: Servant of Turandot ends in andante movement

indicators.note: in says those two letters go inside the rearranged musical term
movement says the letters of andante are moved about

parts.note: a musical tempo marking, taken here as letters

indicators.note: ends takes the first and last letters of Turandot

explanation.surface: A servant in Puccini's opera Turandot performing a slow musical passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like a musical section, fitting andante, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant waits on someone, which is the role of a servant or retainer.

clue.text: Oriental ceremony's held back splendour

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Eastern ceremony's splendour being held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat means brilliance of show or success, a borrowing from French for dazzle and grandeur.

clue.text: Neat way to colour fabric, dropping ends

indicators.note: dropping ends says the final letter of each of the two parts is lost

parts.note: tie-dye is a method of colouring fabric in patterns by tying it before dyeing

explanation.surface: A neat method of dyeing cloth that leaves off the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE-DYE is two words; 'dropping ends' cuts the last E off each.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and orderly are synonyms, describing something kept in good order.

clue.text: Refractory's hot and danger's spreading

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the adjective refractory

indicators.note: spreading says the letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: Something stubborn is hot, and the danger from it is spreading, like a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refractory' suggests heat-resistant material, matching hot, but here it means obstinate.
explanation.definitionFit: A refractory person is stubborn and unmanageable, which is wilful and obstinate.
